newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: ECNZ says looking to raise NZ$400 mln in debt.
newsitem.headline: ECNZ says looking to raise NZ$400 mln in debt.

text.p: Electricity Corporation of New Zealand said on Thursday it would look to raise NZ$400 million in debt in the next month or two in order to raise its gearing to 40 percent.

"The current gearing is less than 40 percent but we will be moving towards that and maintaining 40 percent gearing when the additional capital expenditure is required for the Manapouri extension, and that's about $200 million," Chairman Selwyn Cushing told Reuters after the release of ECNZ's annual result.
ECNZ plans a major upgrade to the Manapouri power station in the South Island.

"Also we are required to pay a special dividend to the government of $158 million and whilst the gearing at this moment is close to 40 percent, clearly it would deteriorate unless we did something to assist the situation.
"We're taking steps in the next month or two to remedy the position so that we're able to attend to those commitments without in any way disturbing our proper businesslike ratios."
He said ECNZ would be in the market for about $400 million.
Asked if the debt-raising would take the form of a bond issue, he said the corporation would look at a number of options.

"That will largely depend on what happens with interest rates and what happens with the international markets and foreign exchange over the next week or two. At this stage it all looks quite promising, although with the government situation
being as it is, everybody is a little reluctant to go for large sums at this moment."
New Zealand currently has a caretaker government after inconclusive elections last weekend.
Cushing said ECNZ would be looking to the international financial markets for the full $400 million.

Asked if there were any alternatives to a bond issue, he said: "If we do see some other products, we will look at them, but we always hedge any foreign exchange contracts so indeed ECNZ do not have to take the currency risk."
